chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the marriage of the Jewish and Christian women. He said: It is not suitable for a Muslim to marry a Jewish woman nor a Christian woman. Only the 'bluteh' (temporary marriage) is permissible from them, and this includes the state of necessity and the absence of a Muslim woman, and this runs in the manner of the permissibility of the meat of the dead animal when there is fear for the life.

key_terms.إِبَاحَةِ لَحْمِ الْمَيْتَةِ: Permissibility of the meat of the dead animal

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a Muslim man marrying a Jewish or Christian woman according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Zurara reports that Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) distinguishes between permanent and temporary marriage, ruling that while permanent union with Jewish and Christian women is generally unsuitable, temporary marriage (nikah al-bluteh) is permissible. This ruling is contextualized by the principle of necessity (darura), where the permissibility extends to situations where a Muslim woman is unavailable, analogous to the consumption of carrion when fearing death. This reflects the Shia juristic view that the restriction is not absolute but subject to specific conditions of need and availability.
